messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we hit an ambiguity in the quota billing path when proxying requests with service-account keys + org-scoped API keys. Customers see tokens billed to project but console shows org usage. Can we decide a deterministic routing rule?
Josh: Quick summary of the problem? I saw an alert but not the full context.
Maya: When request includes both X-Org-ID and a service-account key from a project, our router currently prefers the explicit key -> project billing. But UI wants to show org-level quota if the org header was present and the org has a reserved pool.
Ravi: That mismatch causes double confusion — metrics attribute to project, dashboards show org. Leads to "where did tokens go" tickets.
Tess: Proposal: routing precedence order: 1) explicit project bound key (when present and valid) 2) org-reserved-capacity if header present AND key is permitted to use org pool 3) fall back to hosted default. Basically keep current routing but make attribution mirror it.
Josh: How do we assert "key is permitted to use org pool"? Need a quick API check, not a heavy graph traversal.
Maya: We could add a boolean in key metadata: can_use_org_pool: true/false. Auth service can set on key-create or via an admin toggle. Router reads it from cache.
Ravi: Telemetry ask: emit fields routing.choice and routing.reason for every request. routing.choice ∈ {project, org_pool, hosted_fallback}. routing.reason string should be short: e.g., "key_explicit", "org_requested_but_key_denied", "no_org_pool". That will make dashboard filters trivial.
Tess: UX: console should show the final billing_entity (project:proj-123 or org:org-45) on request-level traces and in the usage table. We can add a column "billing entity" and a small tooltip explaining precedence.
Josh: Edge case: What about delegated tokens where the original owner is different from the bill-to project? Example: service account minted by infra pipeline for org-level runs.
Maya: For delegated tokens we need to propagate origin_project claim. If origin_project != key_project, then we route by origin_project if origin_project has an org_binding and is allowed. Otherwise fallback. This keeps billing aligned with request origin.
Ravi: Implementation notes: router will consult 3 things in order: (A) explicit key metadata (owner_project, can_use_org_pool), (B) request header X-Org-ID and whether that org has reserved pool/permission, (C) origin_project claim if present. We'll add metrics: routing.choice and billing_entity_id.
console-bot: deploy-check queued: auth-cache schema change detected (added can_use_org_pool boolean). Canary to eng-platform cluster in 2h.
Tess: Quick QA checklist for rollout: 1) backend metric emitted for at least 1000 requests, 2) UI column shows consistent billing_entity for those requests, 3) doc blurb + tooltip, 4) migration script to set can_use_org_pool=false by default, and ops toggle to flip for pilot orgs.
Josh: For API, let's define HTTP header fallback semantics in the spec: X-Org-Origin: optional; X-Origin-Project: optional; Authorization: service-key. Router pseudocode in docs: 
```
if key.can_use_org_pool and header.X-Org-Origin and org.has_reserved_pool:
    billing = org:header.X-Org-Origin
elif origin_project present and origin_project != key.project:
    billing = project:origin_project
else:
    billing = project:key.project
```
Ravi: +1. Add metric tag route_trace=true for samples in tracing to debug edge cases.
Maya: I'll open the RFC PR with the pseudocode, telemetry fields, and UI mock. Can we agree to the default semantics so I can finalize?
Tess: Agreed. We should also add an admin console toggle (beta) to override routing for troubleshooting.
Josh: Agreed. I'll take the auth-service change (metadata + admin toggle). Ravi you take router + metrics. Maya/Tess own RFC + UI.
Maya: Awesome — thanks. I'll drop the RFC link here once PR is up.
Maya: (after) PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/812 — includes schema, pseudocode, and canary plan.
Ravi: Noted, watching canary. If we see >0.5% mismatch between billing_entity metric and UI attribution we abort.
Tess: I'll schedule a 30min sync with QA right after canary completes. :thumbsup:
